Journaling Suggestions give you new ways to jumpstart your journaling in Day One. Journaling Suggestions include “Reflections” prompts, media from third-party apps like Spotify and Pocket Casts, State of Mind, and Motion Activity Updates. These help you capture more of life as you live it—whether through your thoughts, emotions, the music you listen to, or the activities you do.

## Getting Started

Journaling Suggestions are available for Day One on iPhone and iPad.

iPhone: Requires Day One version 2024.20 or later and iOS 18 or later.iPad: Requires Day One version 2025.22 or later and iOS 26 or later. In your iPad Settings, go to Privacy & Security > Journaling Suggestions and enable “Allow Sync to iPad.”

1. After updating, go to the Settings App > Privacy & Security > Journaling Suggestions and enable what you want to see in your Suggestions.
2. To get started with any of the new Journaling Suggestions, create a new entry in your Day One journal.
3. On iPhone: Tap the Suggestions icon at the bottom of the screen to view your Journaling Suggestions.
4. On iPad: Access Journaling Suggestions from the side menu > “… More” menu > Quick Start > Suggestions. You can also create a new entry, tap “more” below the start sheet, and tap the Suggestions button. It may take some time for Apple to download your Journaling Suggestions, so check back later if they haven’t loaded yet.

## Reflections Prompts

In addition to the Day One daily writing prompt, you can now view a simple writing prompt that can spark insights or help you process what’s been on your mind. These prompts are embedded directly into your entry, giving you space to expand on your reflections at your own pace. To view a new reflection prompt, you can also tap the refresh icon.

## New Media Sources

Enrich your journaling experience with personalized media suggestions. Now, you might see suggestions based on songs or podcasts you’ve recently listened to from third-party apps like Spotify or Pocket Casts. These suggestions aren’t just random—they’re based on your recent listening habits, helping you connect your journaling to the media that’s been inspiring you lately.

Currently, third-party media suggestions are a static reference in your journal entry. The Journaling Suggestions feature does NOT continuously sync all your listening history. Instead, it selectively offers suggestions based on notable media you’ve consumed. This is not an automatic daily sync of all content from Spotify or Pocket Casts. We’re continuing to explore how to make third-party suggestions more dynamic, such as linking them directly to the Spotify track or Pocket Casts podcast episode.

## State of Mind

The new State of Mind Suggestions integrate with the Health app to help you log your moods and emotions over time. By syncing your logged emotions and moods with your Day One journal, you’ll be able to explore how your mental state connects with your daily experiences.

To get started, visit the Health App > Browse > Mental Wellbeing > State of Mind > Log. From here, you can log an emotion or mood about how you’re feeling in the Health App. Once your Journaling Suggestions refresh over time, you’ll start to see the new State of Mind Journaling Suggestions. Tap the Suggestions to bring them into an entry, where you can write more about your feelings and reflect on your mental wellbeing.

How to Use Day One for Journaling: The Complete Setup Guide That Actually Works – Calmevo

Learning how to use Day One for journaling effectively is simpler than most productivity app guides suggest – Day One is deliberately designed to minimize setup friction and maximize the emotional quality of the journaling experience itself.

Day One is an Apple Design Award winning journaling app with end-to-end encryption, automatic metadata capture, and a warm intimate interface purpose-built for personal reflection. Unlike complex productivity apps that require elaborate configuration Day One delivers its core value almost immediately – the setup decisions that matter are fewer and more focused on personal journaling style than technical configuration.

This guide covers the specific features and daily workflows that make Day One genuinely excellent for sustained journaling practice rather than an enthusiastic two-week experiment that gets abandoned.

---

## Step 1 – How to Use Day One for Journaling: Getting Started

Download Day One from the App Store on iPhone, iPad, or Mac. Day One is Apple-only – there is no Android or Windows version.

Create a free account with your email address. The free account provides access to one journal with basic features – sufficient for evaluating whether Day One suits your journaling style before upgrading to Premium at $2.92/month annual.

After account creation Day One creates your first journal automatically – a default journal called “Journal” that becomes your primary writing space.

---

## Step 2 – Configure Your First Journal

Tap or click on your journal name and select Edit Journal to configure basic settings:

Journal name: Rename from the default “Journal” to something more personal – “Daily Reflections”, your name, or simply the year. The name matters less than the habit but personalizing it creates subtle ownership.

Journal color and icon: Choose a color and icon that feel right for this journal’s purpose. Day One’s visual customization is minor but the emotional association between a specific color and journaling practice creates a consistent psychological cue over time.

Template: Assign a default entry template if you want consistent structure for every entry. Leave blank if you prefer free-form writing. Templates are covered in Step 4 below.

---

## Step 3 – Enable End-to-End Encryption

If you upgrade to Day One Premium enabling end-to-end encryption is the most important security step – particularly for users recording sensitive personal content.

Go to Settings → Sync → Enable End-to-End Encryption. Day One will ask you to create a passphrase – store this passphrase somewhere safe outside Day One. If you lose it Day One cannot recover your encrypted journals.

End-to-end encryption means Day One’s servers store only encrypted data that even Day One cannot read. For users recording mental health struggles, relationship challenges, or other sensitive content this technical guarantee provides meaningful peace of mind beyond standard privacy policies.

---

## Step 4 – Set Up Entry Templates

Templates are Day One’s most underused feature for building consistent journaling practice – they remove the blank page paralysis that stops many daily journal attempts before the first word is written.

Prompt Packs are a new way for you to explore meaningful topics and keep your journaling habit going strong. We know one of the biggest challenges in journaling is simply knowing what to write about. Prompt Packs help remove that barrier by giving you a meaningful starting point each time you open Day One.

Prompt Packs are now available in Day One for iPhone and iPad (version 2025.17) and Day One for Android (version 2025.19). Coming soon to Day One for the web.

## What are Prompt Packs?

Prompt Packs are themed collections of journaling prompts on topics like gratitude, reflection, mindfulness, creativity, and more. Each pack gives you a set of prompts you can answer, track your progress through, and assign to a specific journal. Prompt Packs provide a more guided journaling experience, so instead of facing a blank page, you’re invited to respond, reflect, and explore at your own pace.

## What You Can Do with Prompt Packs

- Browse a growing library of themed journal prompts.
- Save favorites to your personal prompt library.
- Track progress with a visual progress bar for each pack.
- Assign Prompt Packs to specific journals for focused writing.

## Fresh Prompt Packs, Added Regularly

We’ll continue releasing new themed Prompt Packs each month, so you’ll always have fresh ideas to explore and new ways to keep your journaling practice engaging. Each new pack introduces thoughtful prompts designed to spark reflection, inspire creativity, and encourage meaningful writing.

## Language Availability

Prompt Packs are currently available in English only. They’re automatically enabled on devices set to English. If your device is set to another language, you can still try Prompt Packs today by toggling them on in Settings > Prompt Packs. We’re actively working to expand support to more languages in the future.

## Getting Started with Prompt Packs in Day One

To get started with Prompt Packs, you’ll need an iPhone or iPad using Day One (version 2025.17 or higher).

1. After updating to the latest version of Day One, tap the new Prompts tab in the lower toolbar between Journals and More.

1. Browse Prompt Packs by tapping the Prompt Pack name. Try answering a prompt.

1. Add your favorite Prompt Packs to your My Prompts library by tapping the + My Prompts button. Tap Done. Back on the Prompts screen, tap My Prompts to view prompt packs you’ve added to your library.

1. You can also use the three-dot menu. Tap Select Journal to assign the prompt pack to a specific journal.

Tip: Selecting a journal will give the prompt pack the same background color as the color of your selected journal.

1. Once you’ve used Prompt Packs, we’d love your feedback! Let us know what you think here.

## FAQs

What are Prompt Packs?

Prompt Packs are curated collections of themed journal prompts in Day One. They’re designed to help you find inspiration and explore different areas of your life, from gratitude to mindfulness, creativity, and more.

How can Prompt Packs improve my journaling practice?

Prompt Packs give you a clear starting point, helping you move past writer’s block and encouraging you to explore new perspectives. They’re designed to keep your journaling fresh, engaging, and deeply personal.

Where can I find Prompt Packs?
